pages.title: Stable release updates
pages.description: Review, download, verify, and install a published CyRevision release from an in-app prompt.
pages.html:
Releases only#

The updater reads the latest stable GitHub Release for CyRevision. Commits, branches, drafts, and prereleases are never offered as application updates. Project repositories remain independent and do not require GitHub.

Update prompt#

CyRevision checks after startup and displays a prompt when a newer stable version exists. The prompt includes the release notes and offers Later, View release, and Download and install. Check for updates remains available at any time.

Platform package#

CyRevision selects the native installer for the current system: Windows Setup, Linux DEB for x64 or ARM64, or macOS DMG for x64 or ARM64. The release page remains available when a compatible package is not present.

Safe installation#

The package is downloaded into the CyRevision cache. Its SHA-256 value must match the release's SHA256SUMS.txt manifest. CyRevision then schedules an external launcher, stops its background services, and closes completely. The launcher waits for the process to exit before opening the installer. No source-code git pull is performed.

See also

pages.title: Images and binary asset differences
pages.description: Choose text, image or metadata comparison according to the file.
pages.html:
Choose a comparison#

Open Code & Assets > Asset preview & diff, or select a changed file in Changes/History. Choose reference and candidate where offered. Unified and Side by side compare text; Images / Heatmap compares supported rendered images.

Interpret correctly#

Text additions/deletions show changed lines, not full syntax semantics. JSON/INI are text even if generated. Long lines need horizontal scrolling; bounded previews report that they are incomplete.

For images, inspect both versions, dimensions and the heatmap. Pan/zoom/fit helps examine details. A heatmap shows pixel differences, not whether an artistic change is correct. Keep the original dimensions in mind.

Unreal and LFS#

An offline .uasset/.umap preview can show package metadata and detected names, not a complete Unreal-rendered scene. Open the owning editor for faithful rendering. A Git LFS pointer is a small text record describing an object, not the object's image or mesh. Retrieve missing payloads explicitly.

Use Open diff in window or Enlarge to keep the comparison beside another tool. Opening a preview is read-only; restoration/export are separate actions. Do not interpret unavailable preview support as a corrupt asset without verifying it in its source application.

See also

pages.title: Backups, retention, and cold archive
pages.description: Create deduplicated snapshots and copy older content to cheaper mounted storage.
pages.html:
Snapshots#

Choose a backup location and create a snapshot. Files are addressed by SHA-256, so identical content is stored only once. Unreal caches and build outputs are excluded by default.

Retention#

Configure a timeline, maximum version count, maximum age, or storage budget. Retention applies to the active backup store after a snapshot succeeds.

Restore#

Restore into an empty destination whenever possible. CyRevision refuses to overwrite existing files unless an operation explicitly permits it.

Cold archive#

Select a secondary disk, NAS folder, or mounted object storage and choose an archive age. Eligible manifests and missing objects are copied while at least the newest snapshots remain active. Cold archiving is non-destructive and never deletes the active copy automatically.

See also

pages.title: Branches and worktrees
pages.description: Inspect before switching, merging or deleting a branch.
pages.html:
Inspect versus switch#

Open Git > Branches and refresh. Distinguish local from remote-tracking branches. Selecting a row inspects it; switching the working branch is a separate action.

Start work#

  1. Fetch remote references.
  2. Create a descriptively named branch from the intended revision.
  3. Switch and verify the header's branch name.
  4. Commit focused changes, then push to the intended remote.

Preserve uncommitted files before switching. The inspector can browse a branch without changing the checked-out files. A historical worktree creates another checkout and consumes disk space. Close dependent editors before removing a worktree.

Integrate and clean up#

Compare branches before a merge or cherry-pick. Apply dependent commits in order. Resolve or abort an outstanding conflict before another integration.

Delete only a branch you no longer need, never the currently checked-out branch. A merged PR does not prove that every unpushed local commit is disposable. PR > Actions offers confirmed local cleanup when eligible; inspect its target. Local deletion and remote deletion are different operations. Do not force deletion merely because a normal deletion is refused.

See also

pages.title: CI runs and full logs
pages.description: Search full build output, filter errors/warnings and manage eligible runs.
pages.html:
Open a run#

Open Git > CI / Actions, refresh workflows/runs and select one. Jobs load separately. Compare branch, revision and timestamps: an older successful run can coexist with the latest queued/running build.

Read the complete log#

  1. Select a run and job, then open Full log / Logs.
  2. Wait for download/extraction.
  3. Choose All, Errors or Warnings. Search combines with severity filtering.
  4. Use horizontal scrolling or open the enlarged log window for long compiler messages.

Source and line numbers remain visible. Classification is a text heuristic; an empty Errors filter does not prove success. Return to All for context and read the final conclusion. Active, expired or restricted logs can be unavailable; Error summary is not the full log.

Dispatch, rerun and cancel#

Choose workflow and Git ref before dispatch. The workflow must support manual dispatch. Rerun failed applies to eligible completed runs. Cancel requires host Actions/write permission. A job's context menu can cancel the parent run, not just that individual job; read the confirmation. Actions are subject to server authorization even if displayed locally.

PR > CI provides the same log reader/search/filters. Refresh after new commits. Queued or running checks must not be interpreted as success.

See also

pages.title: Code explorer, global search, and AI permissions
pages.description: Browse a complete project tree, search with Ctrl+Shift+F, follow selected-line history, and connect an optional AI agent safely.
pages.html:
Code explorer#

The Code tab shows a hierarchical project tree, file metadata, text previews, and detected symbols. Build outputs, Unreal caches, .git, and dependency caches are excluded automatically. Hidden files remain optional.

Global search#

Press Ctrl+Shift+F from anywhere in CyRevision. Search supports case, whole words, regular expressions, and semicolon-separated patterns such as .cs;.cpp. ripgrep is used when available, with a managed fallback.

Selection history#

Select lines in the preview and choose History of selection. CyRevision follows that inclusive line range through Git. Selecting a folder loads history for the complete subtree.

Optional ai#

Enable AI Workspace from Plugins. Connect Codex CLI, OpenAI Responses API, a compatible API, Ollama, or LM Studio. API keys stay in memory for the current run only.

Permissions#

Read is required. File modification, network access, staging, and commit are separate choices. Codex uses a read-only sandbox unless edits are explicitly allowed. CyRevision brokers stage and commit after a successful run. Push is never automatic.

OpenCode and provider configuration#

The AI provider selector also supports OpenCode CLI. Choose OpenCode, set its executable (opencode or an explicit installed location) and the model/provider configuration expected by your CLI. Codex CLI is a different provider; changing the selector should not keep the wrong executable. APIs and local-model endpoints require their own compatible configuration.

Review a turn#

Choose project context and capabilities, send the prompt, observe the running state and cancel if needed. Review generated diffs and run tests before applying/staging/committing. An isolated worktree is another checkout, not permission to publish. Read the selected provider's status: this guide does not promise identical sandbox enforcement for every external CLI.

See also

pages.title: Explorer, previews and text editing
pages.description: Browse project files and understand preview limits.
pages.html:
Explore#

Open Code & Assets > Solution Explorer. Search a filename or path, choose Tree/List and optionally show hidden files. Refresh explicitly when needed; automatic indexing excludes dependency caches, .git and common generated outputs. A filtered result is not a complete disk inventory.

Preview a file#

Select a row. Text formats including JSON and INI should open as text, with syntax-aware display where supported. Large files use bounded previews and report truncation; the visible excerpt is not the entire file. Binary files show metadata or an appropriate asset preview rather than arbitrary decoded bytes.

Edit deliberately#

Use the editing control offered by the view, inspect the draft and apply/save it explicitly. Changing tabs or a preview selection is not a commit. Check Git > Changes afterward and run format/build checks in the owning tool. Do not assume cross-file Undo or a saved version exists unless the editor provides it.

File actions#

Right-click the selected file for Git / LFS history when Git is active, or Sync history in a supported Sync project. Folder and file histories have different scopes. A selected asset's preview is not its author history; history opens separately. If an action asks you to select a file, reselect the actual file row rather than a directory heading.

See also

pages.title: Console, logs and operation status
pages.description: Distinguish application diagnostics, Git commands and build output.
pages.html:
Where to look#

Code & Assets > Console & Logs contains repository command output and application events. CI build logs live in CI / Actions or PR > CI; Unreal local build logs live in Unreal builds. Choosing the correct source avoids confusing an application warning with a compiler failure.

Investigate#

  1. Note the selected project and the time of the problem.
  2. Filter events by text/severity where offered.
  3. Inspect the related operation and its final state.
  4. Copy only the relevant excerpt for a support report.

The bottom status bar shows the current operation. Task details opens active/recent operations; background updates should not force that panel open. A cancelled scan superseded by newer filesystem events is different from a failed write.

Repository console#

Commands run in the selected repository and can modify files/history. Review commands and parameters; never paste an unexplained destructive command from a log or message. Cancellation requests do not undo a command that already finished.

Logs can contain paths, command arguments and remote output. Redact access credentials and unrelated work before sharing. Clear the view only after preserving the evidence needed to reproduce the issue.

See also

pages.title: CyStore storage contracts
pages.description: Inspect, capture, verify and reconstruct optional chunk-store versions.
pages.html:
Experimental storage#

ICyStorePlugin extends the normal plugin lifecycle. It offers a content-addressed chunk store independently from Git's object database. Ordinary LFS pointers stay compatible, and these methods do not create or rewrite Git commits.

Inspect or initialize the store, capture selected files or tracked LFS files, then list stored versions. The result records distinguish newly written chunks from reused chunks and can report skipped files or warnings.

Verify before reconstructing#

Choose a version ID returned by ListVersionsAsync. Verify it, reconstruct it and read the returned destination and summary before using the bytes. Do not assume reconstruction replaced a working-tree file. Optional IProgress<CyStoreProgress> reports stage, path, byte totals and item totals.

Keep an independent backup while using this Alpha feature.

CyStore workflow

  • ICyStorePlugin.InspectStore
  • ICyStorePlugin.InitializeStoreAsync

  • ICyStorePlugin.CaptureTrackedGitLfsFilesAsync

pages.title: CyStore package versions
pages.description: Inspect published package versions and file manifests.
pages.html:
Open CyStore#

Enable the CyStore provider and open its Alpha workspace for a supported project. Configure the endpoint/project options actually offered, then refresh the version list. Repository versions and application update releases are separate catalogues.

Inspect a version#

  1. Select a version and wait for its manifest/files.
  2. Review names, size and metadata before requesting content.
  3. Choose the intended destination for any supported download/export.
  4. Verify the operation's completion rather than assuming a selected row means installed.

The files list is a manifest, not necessarily a local copy. Availability depends on the configured store and account permissions. An empty list can mean no published version, a filter, a connection failure or insufficient rights; read status before retrying.

Scope and limits#

CyStore is Alpha. Use only the upload/publish/download operations present in the installed provider; it is not a universal marketplace client. Do not overwrite a working engine plugin merely because a package has a higher-looking label. Check compatibility, preserve the previous working version and test the consuming project.

For updating CyRevision itself, use Help > Check for updates instead.

See also

pages.title: Performance diagnostics and safe troubleshooting
pages.description: Gather reproducible evidence and reduce unnecessary background work.
pages.html:
Inspect rather than guess#

Open Extensions & Help > Diagnostics for current metrics and recent samples. Refresh metrics explicitly; Clear samples affects recorded measurements, not the underlying repository. Console & Logs and Task details provide operation context.

Reproduce#

  1. Record the application version, operating system, theme/density and display scaling.
  2. Note the project mode, view, filter and exact action.
  3. Wait for the visible loading state or cancel a genuinely stalled cancellable operation.
  4. Repeat on a small sample project if possible and compare behavior.

Improve responsiveness#

Bound graph/history analysis, narrow searches and avoid repeatedly rescanning generated build output. Prefer exclusions appropriate to the project over disabling all monitoring. Keep cache and build output on disks with sufficient free space. Reduce parallel Unreal builds if CPU/RAM/disk is saturated.

Report a problem#

Include expected versus observed result, a minimal sequence and relevant redacted log excerpts. A screenshot should show the selected view and loading state. Do not delete a repository, backup store or private service profile to fix a UI issue. If the interface appears blocked, check for a confirmation dialog in an auxiliary window and try View > Reset panel layout.

See also

pages.title: Discord project agent
pages.description: Publish grouped Git updates to one Discord channel without requiring GitHub.
pages.html:
Channel webhook#

Create an incoming webhook in the Discord channel that should receive notifications, then paste its URL in the Discord agent tab. A webhook belongs to a specific channel, so CyRevision does not need a global bot token.

Execution modes#

Integrated runs inside the desktop application. Autonomous runs as a multi-project sidecar and continues when the desktop closes. Launch local agent starts the packaged sidecar; a remote server or VPN peer can run the same executable. The control API is Bearer-authenticated, uses loopback by default, requires HTTPS remotely, and allows private HTTP only after explicit trusted-WireGuard approval.

Safe baseline#

The first start records the current HEAD and does not publish old history. Later checks group new commits into one message and can also report active-branch changes. Pulls, peer exchanges, and local commits are detected once they become visible in the local Git repository.

Duplicate prevention#

CyRevision stores a per-project checkpoint only after Discord accepts a message. Run automatic monitoring on a single agent per project; two active agents have independent local checkpoints and may both report the same update.

Secrets and mentions#

The webhook and autonomous control token remain in local user configuration, outside the project and repository. The API never returns the saved webhook. Automatic messages disable Discord mentions.

Limits#

The agent reports Git history visible locally and works without GitHub. Pull requests, issues, and review events belong to a forge and require that forge's own Discord integration.

See also

pages.title: Unity, Godot and Lore integrations
pages.description: Use the correct engine adapter without assuming universal compatibility.
pages.html:
Enable the matching provider#

Open Plugins and enable Unity, Godot or Lore only when needed. Select the project root with the expected engine metadata. Its workspace is shown when the integration is enabled and detection succeeds.

Configure and verify#

  1. Read the detected project/version information.
  2. Choose the external executable or project file requested by that adapter.
  3. Apply configuration and inspect its status before launch/install actions.
  4. Open the owning engine to verify the result.

Each adapter exposes its actual supported controls; this is not a promise of identical features across engines. Do not use an Unreal package installer for a Unity/Godot project. Plugin-side installation and application-side activation are different steps.

Lore mode#

Lore is Alpha and may provide its own operating mode, branch/history or push controls. Treat an Apply/Switch/Push operation as a real project mutation and read its confirmation. Do not infer that Lore history is a Git repository unless the project explicitly uses Git too.

Troubleshoot detection#

Check the selected root, metadata file, enabled provider and visible tabs. Nested engine projects may require registering the actual project folder rather than its parent. Reopen/refresh after external metadata changes. If a version is unsupported, retain the existing project integration rather than forcing a mismatched package.

See also

pages.title: Editor companion connection API
pages.description: Detect engine projects and connect the correct Unity or Godot companion.
pages.html:
Provider contract#

IGameEngineIntegrationPlugin extends ICyRevisionPlugin. It exposes Engine, BridgeStatus and the ProjectChanged event. A change event identifies the engine, project root and action; it is not a Git commit.

Inspect the project before installing its engine-specific companion. Installation and connection configuration can change project-side configuration, so use only the explicitly selected root.

Bridge scope#

The companion uses a private loopback bridge for authorized projects. Detection, installation and change notifications do not imply native asset rendering or semantic differences. File presentation remains an independent contract.

GameEngineIntegrationPluginBase is an optional host-side base class; this reference documents its public contract rather than its implementation.

Engine integrations

Functions#

  • IGameEngineIntegrationPlugin.InspectProject
  • IGameEngineIntegrationPlugin.InstallOrUpdateEditorPluginAsync
  • IGameEngineIntegrationPlugin.ConfigureProjectConnectionAsync

pages.title: Locks and work-in-progress reservations
pages.description: Server locks are different from advisory team notices.
pages.html:
LFS locks#

Open Git > File locks and refresh the server list. Read path, owner, date and whether a lock is yours. Cached entries do not establish that the server is currently reachable.

Coordinate an edit#

  1. Check the current lock before editing a shared binary asset.
  2. Lock the exact path if your workflow requires it.
  3. Edit/test, then commit and push normally.
  4. Unlock when the team can safely resume work.

Unlocking another user's file or all locks needs appropriate authorization. Coordinate first and inspect the confirmation. A commit does not automatically release every remote lock. Enforcement depends on host capabilities and the team's tools.

Advisory reservations#

Team & Network > Work in progress and Unreal Content Browser markers communicate that someone is working on a path. They do not change filesystem permissions, create an LFS lock or prevent writes. Use them for coordination, never as proof of exclusive access.

Refresh stale ownership before overriding a lock. If authorization is refused, resolve account/server permissions rather than deleting unrelated local metadata.

See also

pages.title: Preview and comparison providers
pages.description: Return UI-neutral text, images or metadata for supported files.
pages.html:
Requests and results#

Implement IFilePresentationProvider. ProviderId identifies the provider and Priority controls ordering. FilePreviewRequest contains project root, relative/absolute file paths and size. FileDiffRequest contains project root, relative path and baseline/candidate paths.

Check CanPreview or CanCompare before creating the result. FilePresentationResult describes Text, Image or Metadata presentation, a summary and optional text, image, metadata or baseline/candidate/difference image paths. Return null when no presentation can be supplied.

Keep capabilities honest#

A text preview is not a semantic parser. A binary package fingerprint is not a rendered scene. A Git LFS pointer is not the full asset. Do not claim a renderer or comparison that the provider cannot actually produce.

File previews

  • IFilePresentationProvider.CanPreview
  • IFilePresentationProvider.CanCompare
  • IFilePresentationProvider.CreatePreviewAsync
  • IFilePresentationProvider.CreateDiffAsync

pages.title: Getting started
pages.description: Choose a project mode, register a folder, and understand which tools are optional.
pages.html:
CyRevision keeps Git, synchronization, backups, and VPN independent. Choose only the modules required by the project.

Create a repository#

Use Create repository for a new Git project, or Open repository for an existing one. Add folder registers a folder for Sync or Backup without requiring Git.

Project modes#

• Git: local revision control only. • Git + Sync: local Git plus signed peer exchange. • Sync: current files synchronized without Git. • Sync + Versions: file synchronization with Syncthing versioning. • Backup: deduplicated snapshots without continuous synchronization.

Requirements#

Git and Git LFS are required for Git projects. Syncthing is needed only for a Sync mode. WireGuard is needed only for VPN. CyRevision never starts an optional tool merely because a project was opened.

Native V2 and Classic#

V2 uses a native CyUI interface on Windows. The managed engine owns the same project services; Classic remains available from View > Classic interface and is the cross-platform UI. Both interfaces open the same local CyDoc reader. English is the default and Français is available in Edit > Language or the guide selector.

First session#

  1. Open an existing repository, Clone, Create repository or Add folder as appropriate.
  2. Choose a mode in Overview > Project.
  3. Verify the header's project/branch before an operation.
  4. Review changes before committing, and configure a remote only if publishing is needed.
  5. Set an independent backup and test recovery before relying on team synchronization.

Screenshots use a sample project and may show the English interface or a different theme. Captions and concept diagrams follow the guide language. Use the related chapters for complete procedures.

Use the sample views below to locate projects, history and comparison. The screenshots show the English interface; the explanations and manual are available in both languages.

Interface tour#

See also

pages.title: Line annotations and authorship
pages.description: Trace a line to its commit and read the surrounding change.
pages.html:
Open annotations#

Use Git > Annotations with a tracked text path. Load the context/revision offered by the view. Rows associate text with a commit, author and date.

Investigate#

  1. Locate a line or search the file/path.
  2. Read the commit identity and message.
  3. Open that commit in History for related files and intent.
  4. Compare the earlier revision to understand the actual change.

Blame identifies the latest revision responsible for a line; formatting, moved code and merges can affect attribution. It does not prove who originally designed a feature. Binary assets have no meaningful line blame: use Git / LFS file history instead.

If empty, verify Git is active, the repository-relative path exists in the chosen revision and the file is committed. Newly added uncommitted lines may have no committed author. Renamed paths can require separate history inspection. Refresh after a branch change.

See also

pages.title: Commit network and repository graphs
pages.description: Explore history topology and sampled file relationships.
pages.html:
Analyze#

Open Git > Git graphs, choose commit/file limits and whether to include all branches, then Analyze repository. Start with modest limits on a large repository; these bound work and memory.

Interpret the views#

Commit network shows ancestry and merge lanes. File relations show files changed together in the analyzed sample, not necessarily runtime dependencies. Git activity counts describe that sample, not individual productivity. Unreal dependency results depend on available metadata and parser support, not a full engine load.

Navigate#

Drag to pan. Wheel scrolls vertically; Shift+wheel horizontally and Ctrl+wheel zooms where indicated. Fit or double-click returns the graph to view. Select a node or row to inspect commit metadata. Resize a cramped window.

This local analysis is read-only: it does not fetch, modify the index or rewrite history. If the graph appears empty, check commit count, branch scope and filters, then Fit/reanalyze. A repository without commits has no commit topology.

See also

pages.title: Commit and file history
pages.description: Trace authors, inspect LFS metadata and export historical files.
pages.html:
Commit history#

Open Git > History and search by message, author or hash. Select a revision: the middle panel lists its files and the right panel shows the selected difference. Wait for dependent panels to finish loading after changing the revision.

File history, including LFS#

  1. Open Code & Assets > Solution Explorer.
  2. Select the exact file or asset row.
  3. Right-click > Git / LFS file history.
  4. In the separate window select a commit for author, date, full message and storage details.

LFS versions show pointer OID and expected size. Metadata browsing does not download all historical assets. A missing payload must be obtained explicitly before an export/preview requiring its bytes. Binary assets have commit history, not meaningful line-by-line blame.

Compare or restore#

Choose another revision for an A-to-B comparison. Export creates a separate file. Restore changes the working file: preserve local edits, inspect the destination and commit deliberately afterward.

Resize/reorder columns and scroll horizontally to read long values. An empty history can mean a never-committed file, another branch or an earlier renamed path. Verify the selected repository-relative path before retrying.

See also

pages.title: Repository configuration and remotes
pages.description: Configure the hosting connection without leaving the interface.
pages.html:
Location and prerequisites#

Select a Git project and open Overview > Git repository. Review the root, current branch, repository state and remote list. Registering a folder is not initializing Git.

Add a remote#

  1. Enter its name, usually origin.
  2. Paste the HTTPS or SSH clone URL supplied by the hosting service.
  3. Use Add remote, refresh and verify the fetch/push URLs.
  4. Fetch before choosing an upstream or publishing work.

The URL identifies the repository; credentials or SSH authenticate separately. Do not embed tokens/passwords in URLs. Recognized hosting URLs can open a repository web page. Other hosts or custom URLs may require opening the site manually.

Modify and remove#

Select the exact remote before editing its URL or removing it. Removing the configuration does not delete the hosted repository, but can affect upstream tracking. Recheck branches afterward.

Fetch, Pull and Push#

Fetch updates remote references without merging. Pull integrates the upstream into the current branch. Push publishes commits and can be rejected by authentication, branch protection or divergence. Review the error rather than force-pushing. A local-only Git project remains usable without any remote.

See also

pages.title: Everyday Git workflow
pages.description: Review changes, create commits, work with branches, and inspect history without leaving CyRevision.
pages.html:
Refresh and review#

Refresh reads the repository status. Select a changed file to inspect its diff before staging it. Binary and LFS files are identified explicitly.

Create a revision#

  1. Review the changed files.
  2. Stage all changes or use the repository tools for a narrower selection.
  3. Enter a clear commit message.
  4. Create the revision.

Branches and remotes#

Create or switch local branches from the Branches panel. Fetch downloads remote references without modifying the working tree. Pull integrates the configured remote branch. Push publishes local commits to the standard remote.

History explorer#

Search commits by message, author, or hash. Select two revisions for an A ↔ B comparison. Exporting a historical file writes a separate copy and never changes the working tree.

See also

pages.title: Search code and line history
pages.description: Find text across files with explicit search scope.
pages.html:
Open and scope#

Press Ctrl+Shift+F or open Code & Assets > Code search. Enter text and restrict files with semicolon-separated glob patterns such as .cs;.cpp. Use case-sensitive, whole-word or regular-expression matching only when appropriate.

Follow a result#

  1. Run the search and wait for completion.
  2. Select a result to open the file and matching line.
  3. Inspect surrounding code, not just the matched fragment.
  4. Select a line range for History of selection where available; use file history for whole-file changes.

ripgrep is used when available with a managed fallback. Generated/dependency folders can be excluded by indexing rules. An empty result means no match in the searched scope, not necessarily no matching bytes anywhere on disk. Check patterns, casing, hidden files and exclusions.

Regular expressions#

Start with a literal query before a complex expression. Invalid expressions should be corrected rather than repeatedly retried. Searching is read-only; replacing/editing is a separate operation and must be reviewed before saving. After a branch switch or external edit, refresh indexing if results refer to older content.

See also

pages.title: Ignore rules and tracking patterns
pages.description: Separate generated files, prepared changes and large-file tracking.
pages.html:
Two policies#

Git > Ignore rules handles untracked paths to exclude. Git > Git LFS manages patterns in .gitattributes for content you do want to version. Ignoring and LFS tracking are not interchangeable.

Ignore generated files#

  1. Identify engine caches, temporary files and build output.
  2. Add repository-relative patterns, preferably scoped directories.
  3. Inspect matching paths, save and review the .gitignore diff.
  4. Commit the shared policy only when intended.

Ignoring a previously tracked file does not remove it from the index. Removing tracked generated content is a separate team-visible change; review its scope before committing.

LFS patterns#

Add patterns before committing large assets and confirm Git LFS is installed. Review .gitattributes. Adding a pattern does not migrate old payloads or rewrite history; history migration requires separate coordinated maintenance.

The Changes view's Keep/local-only preparation can exclude items from a prepared commit without deleting them. That choice is not automatically a shared ignore rule. Inspect the included set and staged index before Commit.

See also

pages.title: Keyboard and accessibility
pages.description: Default shortcuts, focus, tables and readable layouts.
pages.html:
Default shortcuts#

  • F1: help for the active view; F5: refresh the project.
  • Ctrl+,: Preferences.
  • Ctrl+O: open repository; Ctrl+Shift+O: add folder.
  • Ctrl+N: create repository; Ctrl+Shift+N: clone.
  • Ctrl+1 / 2 / 3 / 4: Changes / History / Branches / Pull Requests.
  • Ctrl+Shift+F: code search.
  • Ctrl+Alt+F / L / P: Fetch / Pull / Push.
  • Ctrl+Q: request application exit.

Defaults can be customized in Preferences. Operating-system/global shortcuts may intercept a key first. A shortcut is not a bypass for confirmations, missing permissions or incompatible project modes.

Inside this documentation window, Ctrl+K opens global search. Tab and Enter navigate controls; Left/Right collapse or expand topic branches. Escape closes search or reduces an enlarged illustration. These reader controls are separate from the application's configurable shortcuts.

Focus and editing#

Use Tab/Shift+Tab to move through keyboard-navigable controls. Text editors retain their normal editing keys; global commands must not unexpectedly interpret typed text. Commit/cancel a draft explicitly before discarding its context.

Layout and readability#

Resize table columns and windows, use horizontal scroll for long paths/logs and detach dense panels. Increase density/font/DPI settings where supported and choose a high-contrast theme. Color is a supplementary signal: read state labels as well. If a panel goes offscreen, use View > Reset panel layout. Report the platform, display scaling and exact view for persistent clipping.

See also

pages.title: LFS Time Machine
pages.description: Inspect, request, export, and restore large-file versions without silently downloading history.
pages.html:
Track large assets#

Add patterns such as *.uasset, *.umap, *.png, or *.fbx to Git LFS before committing large binary assets.

Storage states#

• Local: the object can be previewed, exported, or restored immediately. • Peer: an authorized device announced the object in a signed inventory. • Archive: the object was detected in the configured cold archive. • Missing: no verified location is currently known.

On-demand requests#

Select a missing historical version and choose Request from peer. The signed request expires after seven days. An authorized peer publishes the object during a later exchange. Interrupted copies resume from a verified partial file and are accepted only after SHA-256 validation.

Restore safety#

Restore changes only the working file. It does not stage, commit, push, or lock the asset automatically.

See also

pages.title: MCP servers and emergency blocking
pages.description: Configure local or remote MCP servers per project and restrict every server or tool.
pages.html:
Transports#

The MCP tab supports STDIO processes and Streamable HTTP addresses. Configure commands, arguments, working directories, environment forwarding, URLs, OAuth, bearer-token environment variables, and HTTP headers. STDIO is available to local Codex providers. Responses API providers use remote HTTP MCP only, require network permission and an explicit tool allow list, and resolve authorization from the configured environment variable.

Tool policy#

Each server has an enabled switch, read-only or read/write capability, network requirement, startup/tool timeout, allow list, deny list, default approval mode, and per-tool approval overrides. The deny list wins after the allow list. API approval requests are never accepted silently; only an explicit Approve policy permits immediate execution.

Project isolation#

Profiles are stored in local CyRevision configuration, outside Git. Block unmanaged Codex servers exposes only the servers listed for the current project. ReadWrite servers require workspace modification permission; HTTP and network servers require network permission.

Emergency block#

BLOCK ALL MCP persists an all-server block and cancels the current CyRevision AI run. Unblock removes the emergency state but keeps individual blocks and permissions. MCP is disabled by default. Prefer environment-variable references for secrets.

See also

pages.title: Members, invitations and roles
pages.description: Separate repository, synchronization and VPN authorization.
pages.html:
Location#

Open Overview > Members. Inspect Git/Sync/VPN participants and authorized peer membership separately. A hosting-service collaborator, a synchronized device and a VPN peer are not the same grant.

Invite a device#

  1. Create the supported single-use invitation.
  2. Transmit its verification code through another trusted channel.
  3. Check the returned device identity and requested role.
  4. Approve explicitly and verify the resulting membership.

Never approve solely because a device name resembles a teammate's. Roles determine allowed project operations; use the minimum required capability. A reachable VPN address alone does not authorize repository or shared-folder access.

Change or revoke#

Review the target device and consequences before changing roles, rotating credentials or revoking membership. Revocation stops future authorized operations; it cannot retrieve copies already delivered to another device. Coordinate device replacement and recovery with the project owner.

If a peer is missing, inspect selected project, invitation expiry, approval state and transport reachability separately. Do not solve membership failures by sharing private peer configuration files.

See also

pages.title: Resolve Git conflicts
pages.description: Complete or abort an integration with deliberate resolutions.
pages.html:
Recognize the operation#

Pull, merge and cherry-pick can stop when Git cannot combine changes. This is not a Syncthing conflict copy. Save editor buffers and inspect the conflicted paths.

Resolve a text file#

  1. Open a conflicted path in the conflict editor.
  2. Compare base/local/incoming versions where available.
  3. Compose the intended result, not merely remove markers.
  4. Save/apply, inspect and test the result.
  5. Mark resolved/stage using the offered action, then finish the original Git operation.

Keeping one side is a decision, not automatic correctness. If uncertain, use the supported Abort control, preserving needed work first. Do not start another integration over an unresolved operation.

Binary and LFS assets#

Text merge cannot combine arbitrary binary assets. Choose a valid version or resolve in the owning application. Obtain the LFS payload if necessary; do not edit its pointer as if it were the asset.

PR conflicts#

PR > Conflicts reports mergeability and paths when the provider exposes them. Some providers only supply a flag, not exact files. Refresh after pushing a fix. An empty list while mergeability is being calculated is not proof of a clean merge.

See also
pages.text: Recognize the operation # Pull, merge and cherry-pick can stop when Git cannot combine changes. This is not a Syncthing conflict copy. Save editor buffers and inspect the conflicted paths. Resolve a text file # Open a conflicted path in the conflict editor. Compare base/local/incoming versions where available. Compose the intended result, not merely remove markers. Save/apply, inspect and test the result. Mark resolved/stage using the offered action, then finish the original Git operation. Keeping one side is a decision, not automatic correctness. If uncertain, use the supported Abort control, preserving needed work first. Do not start another integration over an unresolved operation. Binary and LFS assets # Text merge cannot combine arbitrary binary assets. Choose a valid version or resolve in the owning application. Obtain the LFS payload if necessary; do not edit its pointer as if it were the asset. PR conflicts # PR > Conflicts reports mergeability and paths when the provider exposes them. Some providers only supply a flag, not exact files. Refresh after pushing a fix. An empty list while mergeability is being calculated is not proof of a clean merge. See also

pages.title: Contextual help addresses
pages.description: Open a validated local page, section or illustration from a native host.
pages.html:
Contract#

The native C++ host includes DocumentationLinks.h. bool isLocalDocumentationLink(const std::string& url) accepts the installed reader URL shape and rejects control characters; it is a narrow reader check, not a general filesystem authorization service.

The managed host receives docs.open with topicId, optional anchor and mediaId, and returns a url. IPC id is reserved for request correlation. The host validates the page and section against the installed manifest before opening the browser.

The installed reader is Documentation/Documentation.html; its language/page/section remain in the URL fragment. A path-to-URI API encodes spaces and non-ASCII characters before the fragment is added.

F1 targets the current view without changing the selected project or discarding drafts. A page ID is stable across English and French.

pages.title: Navigation and multiple windows
pages.description: Projects, tabs, tables and detached views.
pages.html:
Projects and workspaces#

The left sidebar contains projects only. Select a project to make it active; its name, branch, mode and counters appear in the header. Groups organize the catalogue without moving files. A scan can continue in the background while another project is selected.

Open a view#

  1. Select a category such as Git or Code & Assets.
  2. Select its second-level tab, for example History or Solution Explorer.
  3. Use View > Detach current tab, the Detach action or a tab's context menu to open an auxiliary window.
  4. Use View > Open windows to focus an existing window or close auxiliary views.

Detached views share the active project's services; they are not independent copies of a repository. Check the project header before an action. Closing a view does not delete project data.

Tables and loading#

Drag a column separator to resize, drag a header to reorder and use the header context menu to hide columns where offered. Horizontal scrolling exposes long paths. Orange identifies the selected tab; action buttons belong to the toolbar. A spinner or loading label indicates an outstanding request. Cancel affects the current cancellable operation, not completed work.

Help#

F1 opens the chapter for the active application view. Help > User guide opens the starting page. Use the global search field at the top, or Ctrl+K, to find a task, setting or API symbol. Expand the topic tree in the sidebar; hover or focus a shortened title to read its full name and description. Use the language and theme selectors without leaving the reader. Reading and sidebar scroll positions are retained when browser storage permits it. CyDoc enlarges illustrations inside the reader; Escape reduces them.

pages.title: Notifications, project identity and licenses
pages.description: Configure catalogue identity and inspect project notices.
pages.html:
Project identity#

Overview > Project provides display name, color and sidebar group. These catalogue settings organize CyRevision; changing the display name does not rename the repository folder or hosted project. Review the displayed path before opening/removing a project.

Notifications#

Overview > Notifications lists the selected project's events. Sidebar badges indicate unread items, not necessarily failures. Read the event type/details and mark handled/read through the offered controls. Task details is the operation history, not the same list as project notifications.

Visible tabs#

Overview > Visible tabs controls which available pages appear. A plugin/mode can make a page unavailable even if you want it visible. Restore visibility rather than resetting all application preferences when only one tab is hidden.

License#

Overview > License shows the project's license information and any supported configuration. CyRevision's application license and third-party notices are separate from the license of your own repository. Review the appropriate license files before distributing plugins or assets. A license label in the interface does not grant rights you do not hold.

Removing a project from the catalogue is not a request to delete its original source files; inspect any optional generated-cache cleanup separately.

See also

pages.title: Perforce workspace
pages.description: Inspect changelists and reconcile with explicit server permissions.
pages.html:
Connect deliberately#

Enable the Perforce integration, select the project and configure the server/client/user settings exposed by the workspace. Confirm the client mapping points at the intended local files. Perforce and Git are different version-control systems; a Git remote is not a Perforce connection.

Inspect before action#

Refresh opened files, pending changelists and file history. Select a path to inspect its current depot/workspace context. Authentication, client mapping and server protections determine available operations.

Sync, reconcile and submit#

  1. Preserve unsaved editor buffers and local work.
  2. Preview the intended sync or reconcile scope.
  3. Confirm only the expected add/edit/delete paths.
  4. Review the changelist and description before Submit.
  5. Verify the server result and refresh the workspace.

Reconcile and Submit are not read-only diagnostics. Avoid applying a broad reconcile to build caches or generated assets. A submit changes the depot and may trigger automation. Resolve server-reported conflicts using the appropriate Perforce workflow rather than Git's conflict controls.

If a command fails, inspect client root, connection/authentication, installed p4 executable and server response. Do not change unrelated filesystem permissions as a substitute for a valid client mapping.

See also

pages.title: Plugin and app API
pages.description: Create project-scoped extensions with explicit file permissions and honest isolation boundaries.
pages.html:
Project activation#

A plugin is enabled independently for every project. Its tabs, project modes, preview providers, and services disappear as soon as it is disabled for the selected project.

Contracts#

Reference CyRevision.Plugin.Abstractions and implement ICyRevisionPlugin. Optional interfaces add file presentation, project modes, AI, game-engine, Lore, Perforce, or project lifecycle capabilities without referencing Avalonia.

File broker#

IPluginProjectFileSandbox grants explicit enumerate, read, and write operations for selected relative roots. It rejects absolute paths, traversal, disallowed roots, oversized content, and symbolic links escaping the project. Writes are atomic.

Security boundary#

An in-process .NET plugin is trusted code and cannot be an operating-system sandbox. Use the file broker for cooperative extensions. Extensions requiring hard network, process, or filesystem isolation must run as an external app or worker process. CyRevision never describes an in-process DLL as fully isolated.

Defaults#

Start read-only, request write/network/process permissions separately, keep secrets out of manifests, and preview destructive or remote actions before execution.

Public reference#

  • Plugin lifecycle and project activation
  • Project file access
  • Issue tracker contracts
  • Plugin-owned project modes
  • Editor companion connection API
  • Preview and comparison providers
  • CyStore storage contracts
  • Contextual help addresses

See also

pages.title: Plugin lifecycle and project activation
pages.description: Initialize a plugin, receive a project context and release resources explicitly.
pages.html:
Lifecycle#

Reference the CyRevision.Plugin.Abstractions assembly and import CyRevision.Plugin.Abstractions. Implement ICyRevisionPlugin, expose its Descriptor, implement InitializeAsync, and release owned resources through IAsyncDisposable.DisposeAsync.

The host supplies CyRevisionPluginContext: ApplicationDirectory, PackageDirectory, ConfigurationDirectory, DataDirectory and ApplicationVersion. Keep configuration and generated data in their intended directories; an application directory is not permission to scan a user's files.

Project context#

Implement IProjectScopedPlugin only when the extension needs a selected project. ActivateProjectAsync receives a PluginProjectSandboxPolicy and a cooperative file broker. DeactivateProjectAsync receives the project ID. Drop project-specific state when that context ends.

A package contains cyrevision-plugin.json, its entry assembly and entry type. Installing a package and enabling it for a project are separate actions. Do not start every optional service just because a project is selected.

Using contracts#

The reference below lists public signatures, parameter meanings and return values. It does not expose implementation files. These contracts are UI-neutral: a plugin does not need an Avalonia or Dear ImGui reference.

File access · Project modes

pages.title: Project file access
pages.description: Enumerate, read and write only within the capabilities granted by the host.
pages.html:
Operations#

Import CyRevision.Plugin.Abstractions. The host passes IPluginProjectFileSandbox during project activation. Its Policy describes the project ID/root, plugin ID, permissions, allowed relative roots and maximum read/write sizes. Default byte budgets in PluginProjectSandboxPolicy are 64 MiB for each operation.

EnumerateFilesAsync needs enumeration permission. ReadAllBytesAsync needs read permission. WriteAllBytesAsync needs write permission. Supply project-relative paths. Absolute paths, traversal, disallowed roots and links escaping the project are rejected. Writes use atomic replacement.

csharp
using CyRevision.Plugin.Abstractions;byte[] data = await files.ReadAllBytesAsync("Config/DefaultEngine.ini", cancellationToken);

This fragment assumes the host already granted that relative root and a read budget large enough for the file.

Boundary#

The broker protects cooperative extensions; it is not an OS isolation boundary for an in-process .NET DLL. An in-process plugin remains trusted code. Requesting network/process capabilities does not create a separate protected process.

Activation

  • IPluginProjectFileSandbox.EnumerateFilesAsync
  • IPluginProjectFileSandbox.ReadAllBytesAsync

pages.title: Plugins and optional features
pages.description: Enable providers explicitly and keep project tools independent.
pages.html:
Locate and enable#

Open Extensions & Help > Plugins. Inspect installed providers, their status and descriptions. Enable only the feature required for your workflow. Most plugins are Alpha; availability does not imply production maturity.

Configure in context#

  1. Enable the provider and apply its configuration.
  2. Select the intended project and inspect project detection.
  3. Open the provider's workspace or plugin operating mode.
  4. Set the external executable/account options, test the connection and inspect status.

A disabled plugin should not start its service just because a project opens. An engine integration can be installed without its external engine currently being running. Disabling an integration does not necessarily uninstall a project-side plugin or remove its stored data.

If a tab is absent#

Check Overview > Visible tabs, the active project mode and file type (.uproject, Unity/Godot metadata or provider-specific project). A plugin-supplied mode can move tabs under its own category. Return to a supported project before assuming the provider failed.

Install only trusted packages. Review compatibility before updating an integration used by a team; close the owning editor when installation requires it. Use the developer API chapter for extension authoring, not application preference files.

See also

pages.title: Preferences, cache, themes and application options
pages.description: Configure global behavior separately from per-project settings.
pages.html:
Open preferences#

Use Edit > Preferences or Ctrl+,. Review Application/Desktop sections and save changes explicitly. Project mode, remote and automatic project services belong to Overview > Project, not global preferences.

Cache location#

Select the cache root using the folder control and read the current path/status. The cache is generated data, not the original repository or a backup store. Changing the preferred root is not permission to delete arbitrary old directories. Stop active readers/transfers before a relocation offered by the interface, verify the new location and inspect disk usage afterward.

Appearance#

Choose a theme preset and density. V2 uses shared CyUI theme roles; the Theme editor allows previewing supported colors. Test selected tabs, disabled actions, diffs and warnings for contrast. Font/DPI behavior depends on the platform; a theme change should not be used to hide an operation error.

Behavior and shortcuts#

Configure startup/tray, refresh/performance and keyboard options that the installed version exposes. Shortcut conflicts must be resolved before saving. Reset a section only when you intend to replace its custom values. Saved preferences do not automatically publish changes or enable every optional project service.

pages.title: Plugin-owned project modes
pages.description: Declare feature switches, retention and supported tabs without coupling to the desktop UI.
pages.html:
Declare modes#

Implement IProjectModeProvider and expose ProjectModes. Each PluginProjectModeDescriptor has an ID, name, description, feature switches, retention, workspace tab IDs and a category label. Mode IDs are unique within the provider.

PluginProjectModeFeatures declares Git, LFS, peer synchronization, backup and standard-remote switches. PluginProjectModeRetention declares current-state, timeline or permanent retention and optional version/age/storage limits.

Evaluate compatibility#

The host passes the selected project's identity, name, root and enabled plugin IDs to EvaluateProjectMode. Return an availability flag and a useful explanation. This check does not switch modes or mutate the project. The provider must be enabled for that project before its modes and registered workspaces are offered.

pages.title: Project modes and service startup
pages.description: Choose independent features for each project.
pages.html:
Location#

Open Overview > Project > Operating mode. This is a per-project setting.

Modes#

  • Git (Beta): Git and LFS; a remote is optional.
  • Git + Sync (Alpha): revision tools plus authorized peer exchange. Synchronization does not replace commits.
  • Sync (Alpha): current-file exchange through a dedicated Syncthing instance, without Git.
  • Sync + Versions (Alpha): synchronization with file versioning, not Git branches.
  • Backup (Alpha): snapshots and retention without continuous synchronization.
  • Plugin modes appear when their provider is enabled. Lore and plugins remain Alpha.

Change safely#

  1. Finish or cancel any operation modifying files.
  2. Select the mode and read its summary.
  3. Apply selected mode and confirm.
  4. Check available tabs and service states.

Existing data is preserved. Active services are stopped/reconfigured; changing mode does not erase stored Git history or backups. Automatic Sync/VPN startup is a separate explicit project setting. Selecting an executable does not start its service.

If an expected tab is missing, inspect enabled plugins, detected project type and Overview > Visible tabs. Hidden/unavailable is different from loading.

pages.title: Pull request manager
pages.description: Review, create, check out, discuss, close, and merge GitHub pull requests inside CyRevision.
pages.html:
Connection#

Select a Git project and open Pull Requests. CyRevision detects the GitHub origin remote. Public repositories can be read without a token; private repositories and write operations use a masked session token or the configured environment variable. Tokens are never persisted.

Review workspace#

Filter open, closed, or all requests. Inspect changed files, unified patches, comments, reviews, branches, draft state, change statistics, and mergeability. Create requests, publish a general comment, approve, request changes, or open the provider page. General reviews and conversation are available; provider capabilities govern line-level actions.

Safe checkout#

Checkout stops when the working tree is dirty. CyRevision fetches the pull head into a dedicated reference and creates or fast-forwards cyrevision/pr-N; it never force-resets the active branch.

Remote actions#

Close, reopen, and merge change the remote repository and require confirmation. Choose merge, squash, or rebase according to repository policy. These actions may trigger CI or deployments.

Providers#

The installed pull-request adapter supports GitHub and a configurable GitHub Enterprise API endpoint. Other hosting services can be Git remotes, but are not supported by this PR screen. Git, LFS, Sync and backup remain usable without a forge.

Tabs, state and sorting#

Description, Files, Conversation, CI, Conflicts and Actions separate the work. Sort PR numbers numerically with the # header. Open/closed/merged state is independent from CI. Author/own-PR markers and colors supplement explicit labels.

CI and conflicts#

Use CI for runs, jobs, complete logs, error/warning filters and text search. Open the log in a separate window for long lines. The current queued/running check must not be hidden by an older successful run. Right-click an active job for cancellation when eligible; the action can cancel its entire parent run and the provider validates permissions. Conflicts reports paths only when the provider/local analysis can supply them.

After merge#

Actions can offer confirmed deletion of the corresponding local branch. Verify that it is not active and contains no needed unpublished work. Linked Jira/ClickUp tasks can be detected and transitioned under the configured/manual policy. A merged PR and an updated task are separate results; inspect both.

See also

pages.title: Remote builds over VPN
pages.description: Run allowlisted builds on a CI machine and download artifacts without pushing a temporary branch.
pages.html:
Agent setup#

Install the packaged BuildAgent on the CI/build machine and run CyRevision.Build.Agent --print-token. The first run creates a token and a safe empty agent.json. Add the exact CyRevision project ID and one or more recipes. The agent operator owns the executable, arguments, timeout, workspace, and artifact patterns; a client can select only a recipe ID and can never submit a command.

Network#

Local testing uses 127.0.0.1:47841. For another peer, bind to the build machine's WireGuard IPv4, add --allow-private-http, and enable Remote build agent over VPN in the firewall assistant. Never forward TCP 47841 on the router.

Source modes#

ExistingWorkspace transfers no source and uses the configured workspace. If both sides have Git metadata, a different HEAD is rejected. UploadedSnapshot sends tracked and non-ignored working files but excludes .git and generated caches, then extracts into a unique path with traversal and size checks.

Run and download#

In Remote builds, enter the VPN endpoint, token, recipe ID, mode, and artifact destination. Test agent lists the allowlisted recipes. Start remote build follows the job log, supports cancellation, and downloads an artifact ZIP after success. Only recipe-declared files and build.log are returned; no commit or branch is pushed to a remote.

See also

pages.title: Multi Restore and cherry-pick composition
pages.description: Compose file versions or ordered commits with a safety preview before changing the working tree or a local branch.
pages.html:
Multi restore#

Open Compose > Multi restore, choose a commit, and load its changed files. Check only the files to include. BeforeCommit selects the state immediately before that commit; AtCommit selects the version stored by the commit. Adds, deletes, and renames become explicit restore or delete operations.

Safety preview#

Build safety preview before applying. The preview expires after fifteen minutes, verifies that HEAD has not moved, detects local changes, and blocks missing Git LFS objects. Application writes a timestamped recovery copy under the Git common directory before changing any path. The index is not modified and no commit or push is created.

Branch comparison#

Open Branch compare & cherry-pick, choose a source and an existing local target. Source-only, target-only, and patch-equivalent commits are shown separately, so an already applied change can be recognized even when its hash differs. Selected source-only commits are applied in the displayed order.

Cherry-pick modes#

KeepCommits preserves individual commits. CombineIntoOne applies their content and creates one commit with the supplied message. Merge commits are blocked until an explicit mainline workflow is available.

Isolation and conflicts#

If the target is not the active branch, CyRevision uses a temporary worktree and leaves the displayed branch untouched. A conflict aborts the operation and restores the target tip. Nothing is pushed automatically.

Detached windows#

View > Open detached workspace opens additional History, Code, Multi Restore, or Cherry-pick windows. Open several at once for multiple monitors; their project data and selection stay linked to the main window.

See also

pages.title: Safe LFS storage and cleanup
pages.description: Move the LFS cache to another disk and reclaim old objects without deleting the project's last copy.
pages.html:
Classification#

Open Git LFS > Storage & safe cleanup and run Analyze. Protected objects are reachable from local refs, stashes, indexes, or worktrees and are never selected. This includes commits and branches that have not been pushed. Eligible objects are orphaned, outside the grace period, and have the configured number of verified copies. Everything else is blocked.

Retention evidence#

A remote copy is accepted only after a Git LFS dry run with remote and unreachable-object verification. A peer copy requires a fresh signed inventory and an object actually published in the exchange store. An archive copy uses CyRevision's manifest and is SHA-256 checked again before deletion. With no remote, retain at least one peer or archive copy; require two or more for stronger redundancy.

Deleted prs and branches#

A branch deleted on a forge may still exist locally. Its objects stay protected until you deliberately remove the local ref. Once orphaned, Analyze decides whether another verified copy makes them eligible. A local-only PR or unpushed branch is always kept.

External storage#

Choose a dedicated empty directory, then relocate. CyRevision copies and hashes every object before setting the repository-local lfs.storage value. A repository ownership marker prevents unsafe shared stores. Keep the old cache for the first test, then enable removal only after checkout and Time Machine access succeed.

Cleanup#

Archive candidates creates verified copies without deleting. Analyze again, review each decision, then confirm cleanup. Plans expire after fifteen minutes, local references are rechecked, and an audit is written under .git/cyrevision/lfs-cleanup.

See also

pages.title: Server HTTP API
pages.description: Use authenticated project, Git, backup, peer, VPN and chat endpoints.
pages.html:
Authentication and responses#

GET /health and GET /api/v1/capabilities do not require an API token. Other /api/v1 routes need the Authorization: Bearer <token> header. This token administers the server; it is separate from signed project membership and WireGuard identity.

Requests/responses use JSON and enum names as strings. Project and peer route IDs are GUIDs. An invalid token returns 401. Known missing-item, denied and invalid-operation errors map to 404, 403 and 400; other failures return 500 problem details. Read the operation result too.

Routes#

Add /api/v1 before each path below. Input names refer to JSON properties unless identified as query parameters.

Method Path Input and result
GET /projects Registered project definitions.
POST /projects name, optional preset/existingPath; 201 and the created project.
DELETE /projects/{projectId} Remove server registration; 204.
GET /projects/{projectId}/git/status Git status, or 204 if unavailable.
GET /projects/{projectId}/git/history Recent revisions.
POST /projects/{projectId}/git/exchange Signed exchange result.
GET /projects/{projectId}/backups Backup entries.
POST /projects/{projectId}/backups Create a backup and return its result.
POST /projects/{projectId}/sync/configure executablePath; dedicated runtime configuration.
POST /projects/{projectId}/sync/start Start service; current state.
POST /projects/{projectId}/sync/pause Pause service; current state.
POST /projects/{projectId}/sync/stop Stop service; current state.
GET /projects/{projectId}/sync/status Synchronization runtime state.
POST /projects/{projectId}/peers/invitations Optional role; exchangeText, verificationCode and expiry.
POST /projects/{projectId}/peers/join-request exchangeText and verificationCode; signed response text.
POST /projects/{projectId}/peers/approve exchangeText; approved membership text.
POST /projects/{projectId}/peers/membership exchangeText; import the signed grant.
GET /projects/{projectId}/peers Authorized members.
DELETE /projects/{projectId}/peers/{deviceId} Revoke the selected device; 204.
POST /projects/{projectId}/vpn/configure Optional networkCidr, localAddress, listenPort, publicEndpoint, capabilities; profile.
GET /projects/{projectId}/vpn/profile VPN profile.
GET /projects/{projectId}/vpn/status Tunnel runtime state.
POST /projects/{projectId}/vpn/start Explicit tunnel start.
POST /projects/{projectId}/vpn/stop Explicit tunnel stop.
POST /projects/{projectId}/vpn/invitations Optional capabilities; signed exchangeText and expiry.
POST /projects/{projectId}/vpn/join exchangeText, optional capabilities; signed response.
POST /projects/{projectId}/vpn/accept exchangeText; accept signed response.
DELETE /projects/{projectId}/vpn/peers/{peerId} Remove the VPN peer; 204.
GET /projects/{projectId}/chat/snapshot Optional user/since query; chat snapshot.
POST /projects/{projectId}/chat/messages Message request; sent-message result.
POST /projects/{projectId}/chat/channels Channel request; created-channel result.
GET /projects/{projectId}/chat/messages/{messageId}/attachment Attachment payload serialized as JSON.

Usage#

Use the presets returned by capabilities instead of assuming every desktop mode is supported. A successful HTTP response does not implicitly authorize a peer: follow invitation, verification and membership. VPN does not replace Git/Sync permissions.

Replace the token placeholder only in your local client. Do not save it in a shared example, URL or public profile.

Configure the server

A successful HTTP response does not implicitly authorize a peer: follow invitation, verification and membership. VPN does not replace Git/Sync permissions. Replace the token placeholder only in your local client. Do not save it in a shared example, URL or public profile. Configure the server

pages.title: Optional server peer
pages.description: Connect an always-available peer without making local Git server-dependent.
pages.html:
When to use it#

CyRevision Server is an optional always-available peer with backups and a web dashboard. Desktop Git remains usable without it. Starting a server does not authorize it for a project.

Prepare a deployment#

Use the supplied deploy/docker-compose.yml and its example environment file. Choose a dedicated data volume and set CYREVISION_SERVER_TOKEN in the deployment's local environment. The dashboard uses port 8080; put an HTTPS reverse proxy in front of it on untrusted networks.

The regular deployment grants no network-administration privilege. Add the VPN compose overlay only if this server must run WireGuard. Git, Sync and Backup do not require that overlay. The supplied systemd unit binds to loopback by default and uses an administrator-managed environment file.

Connect and verify#

  1. Check /health and /api/v1/capabilities.
  2. Open the dashboard and enter the API token for that browser session.
  3. Register the intended project and its server-side location.
  4. Configure and start only the needed Sync or VPN services.
  5. Inspect the final project and service states before exchanging files.

Without a configured token the server creates config/server-token.txt under its data directory. Read it locally as the service owner; never expose it through a public share.

Retention and recovery#

Choose backup storage explicitly. Current synchronized files are not a backup. Keep retention and recovery copies independent, and verify a restore into another folder before removing originals.

pages.title: Shared folders outside the project
pages.description: Share only explicit folders with authorized peers.
pages.html:
Create a share#

Open Team & Network > Shared Sync folders. Choose a specific existing folder, a clear display name and the intended folder policy. Do not share a broad user profile, whole disk or unrelated project just to exchange a few files.

Admit participants#

  1. Check the selected project and authorized peer identity.
  2. Configure the folder's intended participants and policy.
  3. Start the dedicated synchronization service explicitly.
  4. Verify folder/device state and pending changes on each side.

A VPN connection does not grant synchronized-folder access. Adding a device and sharing a folder are distinct permissions. Validate invitations and role changes through the membership workflow.

Resolve and stop#

Inspect conflicts in the Sync conflict view before deleting alternate copies. Pause/Stop affects the project-managed instance, not a personal Syncthing installation. Removing a share configuration is different from deleting its local folder; read confirmations and preserve required content.

Shared current files are not a backup. Use dedicated snapshots for recovery and avoid sharing generated caches that repeatedly trigger rescans.

See also

pages.title: Swarm sessions and secure VPN files
pages.description: Configure Unreal Swarm over WireGuard and exchange files without exposing a public file share.
pages.html:
Swarm session#

Open Swarm over VPN after configuring the project tunnel. Choose Agent or CoordinatorAndAgent, select the matching Unreal executables and existing SwarmAgent.Options.xml, then set coordinator VPN IPv4, local alias, groups, agent filter and optional cache. Apply Agent configuration closes no process: close Swarm Agent yourself first. CyRevision creates a timestamped backup and edits only known fields already present in the XML.

Dns and firewall#

Apply local DNS alias replaces only a marked block belonging to this project in the Windows hosts file. The firewall assistant creates deterministic TCP 8008-8009 rules limited to the WireGuard subnet. Never forward Swarm ports on the modem/router.

Full diagnosis#

Run full diagnosis checks Windows support, the assigned VPN address, executable paths, Agent XML, DNS resolution, project firewall, and both Coordinator ports. Every warning or failure includes a concrete repair step. CyRevisionUnreal also provides Tools > Swarm over VPN for autonomous configuration, process launch and port tests.

Vpn file endpoint#

VPN files binds only to the project WireGuard IPv4 and refuses source addresses outside the project CIDR. Every command requires the 256-bit project token. Choose a private inbox and an explicit shared root, then grant receive, browse and download separately. Send the token to authorized peers through a different trusted channel.

Transfer safety#

Uploads never overwrite an existing file. Uploads and downloads verify the announced size and SHA-256 before an atomic move. Partial files are removed after failure. Absolute paths, parent traversal, junctions and symbolic links cannot escape the shared root. Rotate token immediately revokes old copies and stops the endpoint until restarted.

See also

pages.title: Smart Sync and authorized peers
pages.description: Run an isolated Syncthing instance and exchange signed Git/LFS data with approved devices.
pages.html:
Isolated syncthing#

Each CyRevision project uses its own configuration, database, API key, loopback address, and port. CyRevision never searches for, reconfigures, pauses, or stops a personal Syncthing instance.

Start and stop#

Selecting a Syncthing executable does not start it. Start launches the dedicated project instance. Pause, Resume, and Stop affect only the exact child process created by CyRevision.

Peer admission#

Create a single-use invitation and send its verification code through a separate channel. Approve the returned join request only after checking the device and role. Revocation removes future Git/LFS authorization.

Smart lfs policy#

Current objects are always prioritized. Historical objects can remain on demand, include a configurable number of recent versions, or replicate everything. Signed inventories advertise availability without forcing a download.

See also

pages.title: Sync conflicts and version recovery
pages.description: Resolve concurrent file edits without confusing them with Git merges.
pages.html:
Identify a Sync conflict#

Open Sync > Sync conflicts when the project's synchronization tools are enabled. Concurrent edits can create conflict copies or pending Sync commit conflicts. These are not Git merge markers and should not be resolved blindly through a Git merge command.

Recover deliberately#

  1. Pause editing of the affected file across devices.
  2. Inspect both versions and their timestamps/participants.
  3. Preserve a copy if uncertain, especially for binary assets.
  4. Choose the intended resolution using the offered operation.
  5. Verify the working file and let peers reconcile before resuming edits.

For text, compare content; for binary assets open each candidate in the owning application. A newer timestamp does not guarantee a better version. Sync + Versions may provide older file versions, but its retention is not Git branch history.

Cleanup#

Conflict backup retention and expired-copy cleanup can remove recovery material. Inspect the scope and confirmation first. Test an independent backup restore before relying on synchronization alone: deletions and mistakes can propagate as well as useful changes.

See also

pages.title: CyTask, Jira and ClickUp workflow
pages.description: Configure task providers and verify linked-task transitions after merge.
pages.html:
Enable the provider#

Open Plugins and locate CyTask, Jira or ClickUp. Enable/configure only the installed integration you need. Provider-supplied panels/modes depend on that plugin's capabilities; installing a provider does not connect every project automatically.

Linked tasks in pull requests#

PR > Actions can detect supported task URLs/IDs from PR context such as title, description or branch. Inspect the detected task, provider and project before changing its state. An ambiguous ID alone may need an explicit provider/project mapping.

After merge#

  1. Review the detected references and choose the intended transition.
  2. Prefer manual confirmation while establishing the workflow.
  3. Enable an automatic policy only for a verified project/provider/status mapping.
  4. Merge under the repository's normal permissions.
  5. Check each task update result separately.

A merged PR and a successful task transition are distinct remote operations. One can succeed while the other fails due to permissions, network, missing task or invalid workflow transition. Refresh/check the task before retrying; do not merge again to trigger a task update.

Do not promise a universal Done status: Jira/ClickUp workflows vary by workspace. CyTask's own data and status model can differ from both.

See also

pages.title: Project chat, channels, and private server
pages.description: Discuss in project channels over a VPN, synchronized folder, or your own CyRevision server.
pages.html:
Channel workspace#

The Team chat tab uses project channels, a compact message timeline, attachments, delivery state, and online-member presence. General, development, and builds are available by default. A private server can create additional persistent channels.

Transports#

VPN connects directly to a CyRevision host over a loopback, LAN, or WireGuard address. Sync folder writes immutable per-message files into a synchronized directory and avoids shared-log conflicts. Private server uses the authenticated CyRevision.Server API and keeps the discussion available when team computers are offline.

Private server#

Install CyRevision.Server on a machine you control, set CYREVISION_SERVER_TOKEN, and publish its ASP.NET Core endpoint behind HTTPS. Enter the server URL and token in the project chat settings. Plain HTTP is refused unless the option is explicitly enabled and the address resolves to loopback, LAN, carrier-grade NAT, or a VPN range.

Files and history#

Attachments are size-limited and verified with SHA-256 when stored and downloaded. Server and Sync messages are immutable files grouped by project. Local and synchronized archives can be encrypted. Conversation retention and the attachment limit remain configurable per project.

Security#

Do not publish the direct VPN chat TCP port on a router. For an Internet-facing server, terminate TLS with a trusted certificate and protect the server token like a password. Chat access does not grant Git, Sync, backup, or VPN permissions automatically.

See also
